  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:center;"><a class="rdg-anchor" href="#"></a><a class="rdg-anchor" id="NotestoFinancialStatements" href="#"></a><span style="font-size:9pt;"><b>IMRICOR MEDICAL SYSTEMS, INC.</b>&#160;</span> </p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:center;"><span style="font-size:9pt;">&#160;</span> </p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:center;"><span style="font-size:9pt;"><b>Notes to the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements (Unaudited)</b>&#160;</span> </p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3250822" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c149071923" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i><b>Nature of Operations and Basis of Presentation</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Imricor Medical Systems, Inc. is a U.S.-based medical device company that, along with its wholly-owned subsidiary incorporated in the Netherlands, Imricor B.V. (together, &#8220;Imricor&#8221; and the &#8220;Company&#8221;), seeks to address the current issues with traditional <em style="font: inherit;">x</em>-ray-guided ablation procedures through the development of magnetic resonance ("MR") imaging guided technology. Incorporated in the State of Delaware in <em style="font: inherit;">2006,</em> the Company&#8217;s principal focus is the design, manufacturing, sale, and distribution of MR-compatible products for use in interventional cardiac magnetic resonance (&#8220;iCMR&#8221;) guided ablation procedures. Imricor&#8217;s technology utilizes an intellectual property (&#8220;IP&#8221;) portfolio that includes technology developed in-house, as well as IP originating from Johns Hopkins University, Koninklijke Philips N.V., and livetec Ingenieurbuero, GmbH. The Company is headquartered in Burnsville, Minnesota, where it has development and manufacturing facilities.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company has prepared the accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and notes in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;U.S. GAAP&#8221;) for interim financial information. Accordingly, they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all of the information and disclosures required by U.S. GAAP for complete financial statements. In the opinion of the Company&#8217;s management, the accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements reflect all adjustments, which include normal recurring adjustments, necessary to fairly present the Company&#8217;s unaudited condensed consolidated interim financial information. The accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheet at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>&#160;has been derived from the audited financial statements at that date but does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all of the information and disclosures required by U.S. GAAP for annual financial statements. The results of operations for the interim periods are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the results to be expected for the full year. These unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with the Company&#8217;s audited financial statements and notes thereto for the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, as included in the Company's Registration Statement on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12G</em> filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 18, 2026, </em>as amended by Amendment <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">1,</em> filed on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 24, 2026, </em>and Amendment <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2,</em> filed on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 15, 2026, </em>and effective as of <em style="font: inherit;"> May 18, 2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and notes include the accounts of Imricor Medical Systems, Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Imricor B.V. All intercompany transactions and balances have been eliminated in consolidation.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and notes are presented in United States dollars, unless otherwise noted, which is also the functional currency.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c149071924" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Estimates</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The preparation of unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"> <br/><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c149071925" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i><b>Cash and Cash Equivalents</b></i> </p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Cash and cash equivalents consist of funds in depository accounts, money market funds, and time deposits. The Company considers cash invested in highly liquid financial instruments with original maturities of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less at the date of purchase to be cash equivalents. The Company holds cash with high quality financial institutions and, at times, such balances are in excess of federal insurance limits.</p>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:MarketableSecuritiesPolicy" id="c149071926" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Marketable Securities</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s marketable securities consist of investments in U.S. Treasury bills with original maturities greater than <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months from the date of purchase. These securities are classified as held-to-maturity debt securities because the Company has the positive intent and ability to hold them to maturity. Held-to-maturity securities are recorded at amortized cost, adjusted for any allowance for credit losses, with securities having remaining maturities of less than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year classified as current on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company evaluates held-to-maturity securities for expected credit losses using a qualitative assessment methodology. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c149067664" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesHeldToMaturityAllowanceForCreditLossExcludingAccruedInterest" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> allowance for credit losses was required. U.S. Treasury bills are backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government and are considered to have minimal credit risk.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company excludes accrued interest from the amortized cost basis of held-to-maturity debt securities. Accrued interest totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067665" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesHeldToMaturityAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">59,111</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067666" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesHeldToMaturityAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">117,949</ix:nonFraction> as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively. Accrued interest is included in prepaid expenses and other current assets on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets. The Company recognizes interest income through accretion of the discount from the purchase price to par value over the holding period. Discount accretion is recognized in interest income on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif;font-size:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Fair value is measured using Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs (prices for similar assets or liabilities that are directly or indirectly observable in the marketplace). All held-to-maturity U.S. Treasury bills had remaining maturities of less than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>. Purchases and maturities of held-to-maturity securities are presented within cash flows from investing activities on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="imri:AccountsReceivableAndConcentrationRiskPercentagePolicyTextBlock" id="c149072234" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Accounts Receivable and Customer Concentrations</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Accounts receivable are unsecured, are recorded net of amounts expected for credit losses, and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> bear interest except if a revenue transaction has a significant financing component. The Company reviews the allowance for credit losses by considering factors such as historical experience and current economic conditions that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>affect a customer&#8217;s ability to pay as of the balance sheet date. For current accounts receivable arising from revenue transactions, the Company assumes these factors do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> change over the remaining life of the accounts receivable. Payment is generally due <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> days from the invoice date. When all collection efforts have been exhausted, the account is written off against the related allowance. To date the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> experienced any significant write-offs or significant deterioration of its accounts receivable aging, and therefore, <ix:nonFraction id="c149067673" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivable" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> allowance for credit losses was considered necessary as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had total current and long-term accounts receivable of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c149067674" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsReceivableNet" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">350,288</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c149067675" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsReceivableNet" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">336,539</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of which $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067676" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsReceivableNetNoncurrent" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">95,673</ix:nonFraction>&#160;was included in long-term accounts receivable as of both&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. Accounts receivable includes unbilled receivables of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067677" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnbilledReceivablesCurrent" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">45,757</ix:nonFraction> as of both&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, which represents the current portion of minimum royalties due to the Company within the next <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months from the respective balance sheet date. The long-term accounts receivable relates to minimum royalties due to the Company beyond <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months from the respective balance sheet date.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Raw materials include components used to manufacture the Company&#8217;s capital equipment and consumable products. Long-term inventories represent raw materials and finished goods that the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to consume in production or sell within <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months. The inventories currently classified as long-term are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to expiration.<br/>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company utilizes significant estimates in determining the realizable value of its inventories, including the future revenue forecasts that will result in product sales. These estimates have a corresponding impact on the inventory values recorded as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. Management continually evaluates the likelihood of future sales based on current economic conditions, expiration timing of products, and product design changes prior to sale of product on hand. If actual conditions are less favorable than those the Company has projected, it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>need to increase its reserves for excess and obsolete inventories. Any increases in the Company&#8217;s reserves will adversely impact its results of operations. The establishment of a reserve for excess and obsolete inventories establishes a new cost basis in the inventory. Future sales of inventory on hand at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;will result in recognition of cost of sales based on initial inventory costs, net of reserves taken for expected realization values. For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the Company recorded inventory reserve expense of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067707" contextRef="d_2026-04-01_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InventoryWriteDown" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">213,758</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067708" contextRef="d_2025-04-01_2025-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InventoryWriteDown" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">214,719</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Property and equipment are stated at cost. Additions and improvements that extend the lives of assets are capitalized, while expenditures for repairs and maintenance are expensed as incurred. Depreciation is computed using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets. Amortization of leasehold improvements is computed on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the estimated useful lives of the related assets or life of the lease.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company reviews property and equipment and right-of-use (&#8220;ROU&#8221;) assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be recoverable. If the impairment tests indicate that the carrying value of the asset, or asset group, is greater than the expected undiscounted cash flows to be generated by such asset or asset group, further analysis is performed to determine the fair value of the asset or asset group. To the extent the fair value of the asset or asset group is less than its carrying value, an impairment loss is recognized equal to the amount the carrying value of the asset or asset group exceeds its fair value. The Company generally measures fair value by considering sale prices for similar assets or asset groups, or by discounting estimated future cash flows from such assets or asset groups using an appropriate discount rate. Considerable management judgment is necessary to estimate the fair value of assets or asset groups, and accordingly, actual results could vary significantly from such estimates. Assets to be disposed of would be reported at the lower of the carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell. To date, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognized any impairment loss for property and equipment and ROU assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073531" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Leases</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">At the inception of a contract, the Company determines whether the contract is or contains a lease based on all relevant facts and circumstances. Leases with a term greater than <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months are recognized on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets as ROU assets and corresponding current and non-current lease liabilities. Amounts expected to be paid within <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months are classified as current lease liabilities, with the remainder classified as non-current lease liabilities. The Company has elected <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to recognize leases with terms of <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months or less on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets. Lease payments for short-term leases are recognized as an expense on a straight-line basis over the lease term. The Company includes lease option extensions in the assessment of the lease arrangement when it is reasonably certain the option will be exercised.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">ROU assets and the corresponding lease liabilities are recorded based on the present value of lease payments to be made over the lease term. The discount rate used to calculate the present value is the rate implicit in the lease, or if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> readily determinable, the Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate. The Company&#8217;s incremental borrowing rate is the rate of interest that the Company would have to pay to borrow on a collateralized basis over a similar term, an amount equal to the lease payments in a similar economic environment. Certain adjustments to the ROU asset <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required for items such as initial direct costs or incentives received. See <b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">5</em></b> for additional disclosure on leases.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">For all asset classes of its leases, the Company has elected to account for the lease and non-lease components together for all classes of underlying assets.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:IntangibleAssetsFiniteLivedPolicy" id="c149073534" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Patents</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Expenditures for patent costs are charged to operations as incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073535" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Income Taxes</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Income taxes are recorded under the liability method. Deferred income taxes are provided for temporary differences between financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance to the extent the realization of the related deferred tax asset is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> assured.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company recognizes the financial statement benefit of a tax position only after determining that the relevant tax authority would more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> sustain the position following an audit. For tax positions meeting the more-likely-than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> threshold, the amount recognized in the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements is the largest benefit that has a greater than <em style="font: inherit;">50</em> percent likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c149073536" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Loss per Share</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Basic net loss per share is computed by dividing net loss by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted net loss per share is computed by dividing net loss by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period, after taking into consideration the exercise and issuance of all potential common stock equivalents in computing the weighted-average&#160;number of common shares outstanding, unless their effect is anti-dilutive. Potentially dilutive securities include stock options and warrants, which are evaluated using the treasury stock method, and convertible notes, which are evaluated using the if-converted method.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionsAndTranslationsPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073537" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Foreign Currency Exchange (Losses) Gains</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had cash accounts denominated in Euros and Australian dollars, accounts payable that are denominated in Euros and Australian dollars, lease liabilities denominated in Euros, and accounts receivable denominated in Euros and Hungarian forint. These assets and liabilities have been remeasured into U.S. dollars at period-end exchange rates. Foreign currency exchange (loss) gain of $(<ix:nonFraction id="c149067735" contextRef="d_2026-04-01_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionGainLossBeforeTax" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">683,434</ix:nonFraction>)&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067736" contextRef="d_2025-04-01_2025-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionGainLossBeforeTax" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,285,261</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively, and $(<ix:nonFraction id="c149067739" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionGainLossBeforeTax" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">281,024</ix:nonFraction>)&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067740" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionGainLossBeforeTax" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,159,493</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively, are included on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations within other income (expense).</p>

   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073538" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Revenue Recognition</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In order for an arrangement to be considered a contract, it must be probable that the Company will collect the consideration to which it is entitled for goods or services to be transferred. The Company then assesses the goods or services promised within the contract to determine whether each promised good or service is a performance obligation. Performance obligations are promises in a contract to transfer a distinct good or service to the customer that (i) the customer can benefit from on its own or together with other readily available resources, and (ii) is separately identifiable from other promises in the contract.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company determines the transaction price based on the amount of consideration the Company expects to receive for providing the promised goods or services in the contract. Consideration <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be fixed, variable, or a combination of both.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">At contract inception for arrangements that include variable consideration, the Company estimates the probability and extent of consideration it expects to receive under the contract utilizing either the most likely amount method or expected amount method, whichever best estimates the amount expected to be received. The Company then considers any constraints on the variable consideration and includes in the transaction price variable consideration to the extent it is deemed probable that a significant reversal in the amount of cumulative revenue recognized will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> occur when the uncertainty associated with the variable consideration is subsequently resolved.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s product revenue is derived from sales of both capital equipment and single use consumables used in iCMR-guided cardiac ablation procedures. Capital equipment includes the Company&#8217;s systems such as the Advantage-MR EP Recorder/Stimulator System and NorthStar Mapping System as well as related <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party equipment, while consumables primarily comprise the Company&#8217;s catheters, including the Vision-MR Ablation Catheter and Vision-MR Diagnostic Catheter, and related accessories.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">For equipment and consumable product sales that contain a single performance obligation, the Company recognizes revenue when control is transferred to the customer. This occurs at a point in time when title to the goods and risk of loss transfers. The transaction price is based on invoice price, net of any variable consideration.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">When accounting for a contract that contains multiple performance obligations, the Company must develop judgmental assumptions to determine the estimated standalone selling price (&#8220;SSP&#8221;) for each performance obligation identified in the contract. The Company utilizes the observable SSP when available, which represents the price charged for the promised product or service when sold separately. When the SSP for the Company&#8217;s products or services are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> directly observable, the Company determines the SSP using relevant information available and applies suitable estimation methods including, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, the cost-plus margin approach. The Company then allocates the transaction price to each performance obligation based on the relative SSP and recognizes as revenue the amount of the transaction price that is allocated to the respective performance obligation when (or as) control is transferred to the customer and the performance obligation is satisfied.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Revenue from service contracts is recognized over the contract period on a straight-line basis, as the customer benefits from the services throughout the service contract period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Revenue is derived from both domestic and foreign countries. Sales tax and value added taxes in foreign jurisdictions that are collected from customers and remitted to governmental authorities are accounted for on a net basis and therefore are excluded from net sales. Product sales include shipment and handling fees charged to customers. Shipping and handling costs associated with outbound freight after control over a product has transferred to a customer are accounted for as a fulfillment cost and are included in cost of goods sold.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067748" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationExpectedTimingOfSatisfactionStartDateAxis-date.domain-2026-07-01" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligation" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">129,794</ix:nonFraction> of a contract&#8217;s transaction price was allocated to an unsatisfied performance obligation. The Company expects to recognize the revenue related to this performance obligation during <em style="font: inherit;"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068157">2027.</span></em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="imri:RoyaltiesRevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073539" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Royalties</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2012, </em>the Company licensed certain intellectual property to a customer which included a royalty of <ix:nonFraction id="c149067750" contextRef="i_2012-06-01" unitRef="Pure" name="imri:RoyaltyPercentOfSales" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">3</ix:nonFraction>% of product sales, subject to a minimum of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067751" contextRef="d_2012-06-01_2012-06-01" unitRef="USD" name="imri:MinimumGuaranteedRoyaltiesIncomePerYear" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">50,000</ix:nonFraction> per year through <em style="font: inherit;">2028.</em> The minimum guaranteed royalties were recognized upon the execution of the license agreement as these proceeds were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> variable consideration. The remaining minimum royalty payments to be received, less the portion which represents future interest expected to be received within <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months is included in Accounts receivable and the amounts expected to be received in future periods beyond <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months are included in Accounts receivable, long term. Any royalties received in the future which are more than the minimum guaranteed royalty will be recognized when they are earned.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;&#8195;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="imri:ContractLiabilitiesPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073540" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Contract Liabilities</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2013,</em> the Company licensed certain intellectual property to a customer in exchange for an upfront non-refundable license fee and milestone payments, which can total up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067757" contextRef="i_2013-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="imri:LicensingAgreementMaximumLicenseFeeAndMilestonePayments" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">7,000,000</ix:nonFraction>. The Company collected $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067758" contextRef="i_2016-10-31" unitRef="USD" name="imri:LicensingAgreementRecognized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">6,000,000</ix:nonFraction> of these milestone payments, including the non-refundable license fee, on or before <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2016. </em>A total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067759" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-LicenseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">373,333</ix:nonFraction> of this amount is deferred as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. The customer sold the portion of the business which held this license in <em style="font: inherit;"> May 2018, </em>and the license has been assigned to the purchaser. The project is still on hold with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> plans to work on final development during the next <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months, and therefore, the contract liability is included in long-term liabilities on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company invoices its customers for product revenue based on the billing schedules in its sales arrangements. Service contracts are billed in advance, prior to the services having been performed, and the associated deferred revenue is recognized over the term of the service contract period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Amounts received prior to satisfying the above revenue recognition criteria are recorded as contract liabilities on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets, with the contract liabilities to be recognized beyond <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year being classified as non-current contract liabilities. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had total current and long-term contract liabilities of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c149067764" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,116,132</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c149067765" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,119,788</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, of which $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067766" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityNoncurrent" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,085,753</ix:nonFraction>&#160;was included in long-term liabilities as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>, the Company expects to recognize the balance included in long-term liabilities at an indeterminable time because a portion of the balance relates to milestone payments for a project that is currently on hold, as discussed above, while recognition of the remaining balance is contingent upon obtaining certain regulatory approvals. The decrease in contract liabilities is due to recognition of revenue for completion of performance obligations that were included in contract liabilities at the beginning of the period.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073541" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Derivative Asset, Option Liabilities, and Warrant Liabilities</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Capital Commitment Agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with GEM Global Yield LLC SCS (&#8220;GGY&#8221;) (discussed further in Note <em style="font: inherit;">8</em>) meets the definition of a derivative and was recorded upon issuance within other assets on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The derivative asset is revalued at each balance sheet date, with changes in fair value recorded on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations as other income (expense). The Company estimates the fair value of the asset using the Monte Carlo Simulation model.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Also, in connection with the Agreement with GGY, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c149067769" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:OptionIndexedToIssuersEquityIndexedShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5,700,000</ix:nonFraction> options which were determined to qualify as liabilities in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">480</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10,</em> Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity and ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40,</em> Derivatives and Hedging. Additionally, the Company issued warrants in connection with the equity raises in <em style="font: inherit;"> August </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> October 2023 (</em>Note <em style="font: inherit;">9</em>), where <ix:nonFraction id="c149067775" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-LiabilityWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,100,568</ix:nonFraction> warrants were determined to qualify as liabilities due to the exercise price being denominated in a currency other than the Company&#8217;s functional currency. The result of this accounting treatment is that the options and warrants are recorded upon issuance as liabilities on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets at fair value and are revalued at each balance sheet date, with the change in fair value recorded on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations as other income (expense). The Company estimates the fair value of the liabilities using the Black-Scholes pricing model.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">See <b>Notes <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">9</em></b> for further details and assumptions used in the Black-Scholes pricing model and Monte Carlo Simulation model.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman, Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c149073542" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Stock-Based Compensation</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company measures and records compensation expense using the applicable accounting guidance for share-based payments related to equity awards granted to directors and employees. The fair value of stock options, including performance awards, without a market condition is estimated at the date of grant, using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. The fair value of stock options with a market condition is estimated at the date of grant using the Monte Carlo Simulation model. The Black-Scholes and Monte Carlo Simulation valuation models incorporate assumptions as to stock price volatility, the expected life of options or awards, a risk-free interest rate, and dividend yield.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s policy is to account for forfeitures as they occur and compensation expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the vesting period for awards with service and market conditions; for awards with performance conditions, expense is recognized over the requisite service period for awards for which the performance condition is considered probable of being achieved. Compensation expense is recognized for all awards over the vesting period to the extent the employees or directors meet the requisite service requirements, whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the award is ultimately exercised. Conversely, when an employee or director does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the requisite service requirements and forfeits the award prior to vesting, any compensation expense previously recognized for the award is reversed.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">See <b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">9</em></b> for further details and assumptions used in the Black-Scholes pricing model.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"></p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073543" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Fair Value Measurement</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> Fair Value Measurements, (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820&#8221;</em>) provides guidance on the development and disclosure of fair value measurements. Under this accounting guidance, fair value is defined as an exit price, representing the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. As such, fair value is a market-based measurement that should be determined based on assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or a liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The accounting guidance classifies fair value measurements in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the following <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> categories for disclosure purposes:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table style="border-collapse:collapse;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;height:auto;width:100%;"><tbody><tr style="background-color:#cceeff;"><td style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:3%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></td><td class="ck-editor__editable ck-editor__nested-editable" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:8%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em>&#160;</p></td><td style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:89%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</span></p></td></tr>
<tr style="background-color:#ffffff;"><td style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:3%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></td><td class="ck-editor__editable ck-editor__nested-editable" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:8%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em>&#160;</p></td><td style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:89%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Inputs other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> prices for similar assets or liabilities that are directly or indirectly observable in the marketplace.</span></p></td></tr>
<tr style="background-color:#cceeff;"><td style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:3%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></td><td class="ck-editor__editable ck-editor__nested-editable" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:8%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em>&#160;</p></td><td style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;padding:0px;vertical-align:top;width:89%;"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;">Unobservable inputs which are supported by little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market activity and values determined using pricing models, discounted cash flow methodologies, or similar techniques, as well as instruments for which the determination of fair value requires significant judgment or estimation.</span></p></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company evaluates assets and liabilities subject to fair value measurements on a recurring basis to determine the appropriate level at which to classify them for each reporting period. This determination requires significant judgments to be made by the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The carrying value of financial assets and liabilities recorded at fair value is measured on a recurring or nonrecurring basis. Financial assets and liabilities measured on a non-recurring basis are those that are adjusted to fair value when a significant event occurs. The Company had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> financial assets or liabilities carried and measured on a nonrecurring basis during the reporting periods. Financial assets and liabilities measured on a recurring basis are those that are adjusted to fair value each time a financial statement is prepared. The following tables present information about the Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis, based on the fair value hierarchy:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

The Company estimates the fair value of the asset or liabilities using the Monte Carlo Simulation model or Black-Scholes pricing model.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistancePolicyTextBlock" id="c149073544" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Bioscience Innovation Grant</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2023, </em>the Company received a $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067801" contextRef="i_2023-08-31_GovernmentAssistanceTypeAxis-BioscienceInnovationGrantMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceAwardAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,158,000</ix:nonFraction> grant from the North Dakota Department of Agriculture as part of the department&#8217;s Bioscience Innovation Grant (&#8220;BIG") program. The grant money is obtained by submitting requests for reimbursement of specific expenses incurred to support the remaining approval process of the Company&#8217;s products in the US.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company has elected to account for the reimbursement as a government grant. U.S. GAAP does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently include grant accounting guidance that is in effect related to transfers of assets from governments to business entities, therefore, the Company has elected to follow the grant accounting model in International Accounting Standard (&#8220;IAS&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> Accounting for Government Grants and Disclosure of Government Assistance. In accordance with IAS <em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> the Company cannot recognize any income from the grant until there is reasonable assurance (similar to the &#8220;probable&#8221; threshold in U.S. GAAP) that any conditions attached to the grant will be met and that the grant will be received. Once it is reasonably assured that the grant conditions will be met and that the grant will be received, grant income is recorded on a systematic basis over the periods in which the Company incurred the reimbursable expenses for which the grant is intended to compensate. Income from the grant can be presented as either other income or as a reduction in the expenses for which the grant was intended to compensate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The grant program ended on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025. </em>Income of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067805" contextRef="d_2025-04-01_2025-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceNonoperatingIncome" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">248,373</ix:nonFraction> for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025</em>, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067807" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceNonoperatingIncome" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">658,546</ix:nonFraction> for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025</em>, was included in government grant income on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><i><b>The Dutch Research and Development Act Grant</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 2pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2026, </em>the Company received a $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067809" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_GovernmentAssistanceTypeAxis-TheDutchResearchAndDevelopmentActGrantMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceAwardAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">34,814</ix:nonFraction> grant from the Dutch Research and Development Act ("WBSO"). The WBSO provides compensation for a part of research and development wages and other costs through a reduction in payroll taxes.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:0pt;">The Company has elected to account for the reimbursement as a government grant. U.S. GAAP does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently include grant accounting guidance that is in effect related to transfers of assets from governments to business entities, therefore, the Company has elected to follow the grant accounting model in International Accounting Standard (&#8220;IAS&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> Accounting for Government Grants and Disclosure of Government Assistance. In accordance with IAS <em style="font: inherit;">20,</em> the Company cannot recognize any income from the grant until there is reasonable assurance (similar to the &#8220;probable&#8221; threshold in U.S. GAAP) that any conditions attached to the grant will be met and that the grant will be received. Once it is reasonably assured that the grant conditions will be met and that the grant will be received, grant income is recorded on a systematic basis over the periods in which the Company incurred the reimbursable expenses for which the grant is intended to compensate. Income from the grant can be presented as either other income or as a reduction in the expenses for which the grant was intended to compensate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0;margin-left:0;margin-right:0;margin-top:0;text-align:justify;text-indent:0pt;">Income of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067813" contextRef="d_2026-04-01_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceNonoperatingIncome" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">34,814</ix:nonFraction> was included in government grant income on the unaudited condensed statements of operations for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 2pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 2pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c149073546" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company considers the applicability and impact of all Accounting Standard Updates (&#8220;ASUs&#8221;). ASUs <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> discussed below were assessed and determined to be either <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> applicable or are expected to have minimal impact on the Company&#8217;s unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and related notes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2025, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05,</em> Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets, which provides a practical expedient for entities estimated expected credit losses on current accounts receivable and current contract assets arising from transactions under Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606.</em> The practical expedient permits an entity to assume current conditions as of the balance sheet date that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> change for the remaining life of the current accounts receivable and current contract assets. The Company adopted this standard as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2026, </em>on a prospective basis and elected the practical expedient for all in scope current trade receivables and current contract assets. Adoption of the ASU did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">04,</em> Debt &#8211; Debt with Conversion and Other Options (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">470</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em>), which amends ASC <em style="font: inherit;">470</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">20</em> to clarify the circumstances in which an entity is required to account for a settlement of a debt instrument as an induced conversion. The Company adopted this standard as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2026, </em>prospectively. Adoption of the ASU did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
