   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> Income Statement &#8211; Reporting Comprehensive Income &#8211; Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>). The amendment requires disaggregated disclosure of income statement expenses for public business entities (&#8220;PBEs&#8221;). The ASU does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> change the expense captions an entity presents on the face of the income statement; rather, it requires disaggregation of certain expense captions into specified categories in disclosures within the footnotes to the financial statements. The standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>Early adoption is permitted. The Company is currently assessing the potential impact of adopting this new guidance on our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10,</em> Government Grants (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">832</em>): Accounting for Government Grants Received by Business Entities, which establishes recognition, measurement, and presentation guidance for government grants received by business entities, distinguishing between grants related to assets and grants related to income. The guidance requires a government grant to be recognized when it is probable that the entity will comply with the conditions of the grant and that the grant will be received. The standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2028, </em>for public business entities, and after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2029, </em>for all other entities, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently assessing the potential impact of adopting this new guidance on our interim unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>): Narrow-Scope Improvements, which clarifies interim disclosure requirements and the applicability of Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270,</em> resulting in a consolidated list of all interim disclosures required by U.S. GAAP. The amendments include a disclosure principle that requires entities to disclose events since the end of the last annual reporting period that have a material impact on the entity. The standard is effective for interim periods within fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>for public business entities, and after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2028, </em>for all other entities, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently assessing the potential impact of adopting this new guidance on our interim unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> </b>&#8211;<b> Liquidity</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements have been prepared on a going concern basis, which contemplates the realization of assets and satisfaction of liabilities and commitments in the normal course of business.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">At each reporting period, the Company evaluates whether conditions or events raise substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern for <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year after the date that the financial statements are available to be issued. In performing this evaluation, management considers the Company&#8217;s current financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, contractual obligations, and its ability to obtain additional financing if needed.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>, the Company incurred net losses of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067847" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">25,138,772</ix:nonFraction>, and cash used for operating activities was $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067848" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">14,032,058</ix:nonFraction>. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>, the Company had working capital of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067849" contextRef="i_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="imri:WorkingCapital" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">29,105,091</ix:nonFraction>. Current liabilities include the current portions of the Company&#8217;s convertible notes (related party) and option liabilities, which are recorded at fair value in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">825</em> and ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em> respectively, and their carrying amounts <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ significantly from the contractual principal and interest or other cash obligations associated with settling these instruments. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em> for disclosure of the contractual principal and interest outstanding on the Company&#8217;s convertible notes (related party) as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Management has evaluated the principal conditions affecting the Company&#8217;s liquidity, including recurring operating losses, cash used for operating activities, and contractual obligations due within the next <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months. Based on this evaluation management has concluded that the Company has sufficient liquidity to fund its operations and meet its obligations as they become due for at least the <em style="font: inherit;">12</em>-month period following the date the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements are available to be issued.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">6</em> </b>&#8211;<b> Commitments and Contingencies</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Vendor concentration</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s products include components that are manufactured and supplied by <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties. Certain components and products that meet the Company&#8217;s requirements are available only from a single supplier or a limited number of suppliers. This concentration creates potential for disruptions, which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include issues with availability of product components and pricing. Shortages of product components, quality control problems, production capacity constraints, or delays by suppliers could negatively affect the Company&#8217;s ability to meet its production goals, which in turn could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition, and results of operations. The Company believes that it will be able to source alternative suppliers or materials if required to do so.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">At&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>, the Company had accounts payable to a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068161">vendor</span> that accounted for <ix:nonFraction id="c149067870" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsPayableBenchmarkMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-SupplierConcentrationRiskMember_ShareBasedGoodsAndNonemployeeServicesTransactionBySupplierAxis-VendorOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">32</ix:nonFraction>% of the total outstanding balance. For the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had accounts payable to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149067871">two</span> vendors that each accounted for <ix:nonFraction id="c149067872" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ConcentrationRiskByBenchmarkAxis-AccountsPayableBenchmarkMember_ConcentrationRiskByTypeAxis-SupplierConcentrationRiskMember_ShareBasedGoodsAndNonemployeeServicesTransactionBySupplierAxis-VendorOneMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskPercentage1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">12</ix:nonFraction>% of the total outstanding balance.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The maturity date on the notes is the earliest occurrence of (i) a change-in-control event, at which time the Company would be required to pay the holder the greater of <ix:nonFraction id="c149067937" contextRef="i_2022-12-16_DebtInstrumentAxis-SecuritiesPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="imri:DebtInstrumentPercentOfOutstandingBalancePayableOnChangeincontrol" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">125</ix:nonFraction>% of the then outstanding balance plus accrued and unpaid interest or the amount the holder would receive if the principal and accrued and unpaid interest had been converted to CDIs at a conversion price equal to the variable weighted average price (&#8220;VWAP&#8221;) of the CDIs for the <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> day period ending on the change-in-control event date; or (ii) the <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> year anniversary of the closing date of each tranche.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 28, 2023 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 23, 2022, </em>pursuant to the Securities Purchase Agreement, the Company issued warrants exercisable for <ix:nonFraction id="c149067940" contextRef="i_2023-03-28_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-SpaWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,043,699</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction id="c149067941" contextRef="i_2022-12-23_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-SpaWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">907,141</ix:nonFraction> CDIs, respectively, with an exercise price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067942" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-SpaWarrantsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightExercisePriceOfWarrantsOrRights1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.2563</ix:nonFraction> per share. The warrants expire <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149067943">five</span> years after the dates of issuance.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company accounts for its convertible promissory notes under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em> Derivatives and Hedging ("ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815"</em>). Under <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">15</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">25,</em> the election can be made at the inception of a financial instrument to account for the instrument under the fair value option under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">825.</em> The Company has made such election for its convertible promissory notes because the notes contain conversion and settlement features and management believes that measuring the entire instrument at fair value provides more relevant information about the current value of the obligation and changes in that value over time. Using the fair value option, the convertible promissory notes are required to be recorded at their initial fair value on the date of issuance, and each balance sheet date thereafter. Changes in the estimated fair value of the notes are recognized as a non-cash item in the change in fair value of convertible notes (related party) on the unaudited condensed consolidated statements of operations.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Significant assumptions used to determine the fair value of the convertible note include the estimated probability of a change in control event, which is based on management&#8217;s expectation of future transactions; the volatility of the stock price, which is estimated based on the Company&#8217;s own historical volatility; and the credit spread, which is based on the Company's estimate of its credit rating derived from the Company's financial condition and market yields for similar instruments issued by companies with comparable credit ratings.<br/>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company evaluated the warrants under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">480,</em> Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">480&#8221;</em>) and ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815.</em> The warrants do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the characteristics for liability classification under either provision and as such are classified as equity under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815.</em> Given that the convertible notes were subject to fair value remeasurement, the fair value of the convertible notes was carved out from gross proceeds and the remainder of the gross proceeds of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> tranches of $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067964" contextRef="d_2022-12-23_2022-12-23_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-SpaWarrantsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdjustmentsToAdditionalPaidInCapitalWarrantIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">127,900</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c149067965" contextRef="d_2023-03-28_2023-03-28_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-SpaWarrantsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AdjustmentsToAdditionalPaidInCapitalWarrantIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">541,200</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, was allocated to warrants. The warrants were recorded as Additional paid-in capital on the unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets at the dates of issuance. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> subsequent remeasurement of the warrants is required.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> </b>&#8211;<b> Capital Commitments</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 6, 2023, </em>the Company entered into a Capital Commitment Agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with GEM Global Yield LLC SCS (&#8220;GGY&#8221;), under the terms of which GGY has agreed to provide the Company with up to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149067968">$30</span> million Australian dollars through a Security Subscription Facility (the &#8220;Facility&#8221;) over a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2023-07-06_CreditFacilityAxis-LineOfCreditMember_LineOfCreditFacilityAxis-GemGlobalYieldGgyMember" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtTerm" id="c149067969" format="ixt-sec:duryear">3</ix:nonNumeric>-year term. The Agreement allows the Company to draw down funds during the <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2023-07-06_CreditFacilityAxis-LineOfCreditMember_LineOfCreditFacilityAxis-GemGlobalYieldGgyMember" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtTerm" id="c149067970" format="ixt-sec:duryear">3</ix:nonNumeric>-year term by giving GGY <em style="font: inherit;">15</em> Australian Securities Exchange (&#8220;ASX&#8221;) trading days&#8217; notice to subscribe for CDIs, subject to share lending arrangement(s) being in place. The number of CDIs which GGY <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>subscribe for is capped at <ix:nonFraction id="c149067972" contextRef="i_2023-07-06_CreditFacilityAxis-LineOfCreditMember_LineOfCreditFacilityAxis-GemGlobalYieldGgyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="imri:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumPercentOfCdisSubscribeable" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">700</ix:nonFraction>% of the average daily number of CDIs traded on the ASX during the <em style="font: inherit;">15</em> trading days prior to the relevant drawdown notice, subject to certain adjustments. The subscription price of the CDIs to be issued to GGY is the higher of (i) <ix:nonFraction id="c149067974" contextRef="i_2023-07-06_CreditFacilityAxis-LineOfCreditMember_LineOfCreditFacilityAxis-GemGlobalYieldGgyMember" unitRef="Pure" name="imri:LineOfCreditFacilitySubscriptionPriceOfCdisPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">90</ix:nonFraction>% of the average closing bid price of the Company&#8217;s CDIs over the <em style="font: inherit;">15</em> consecutive trading days after the Company gives the drawdown notice, subject to certain adjustments; or (ii) a fixed floor price nominated by the Company in the drawdown notice. The Company controls the timing of drawdowns under the Facility and has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> minimum drawdown obligation. The issue of CDIs to GGY pursuant to any drawdown notice will also be conditional on the Company having sufficient placement capacity under ASX Listing Rules <em style="font: inherit;">7.1</em> or <em style="font: inherit;">7.1A</em> (as applicable) or obtaining any requisite securityholder approval for the issue.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Common Stock</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Australian Securities Exchange (&#8220;ASX&#8221;) uses an electronic system called CHESS for the clearance and settlement of trades on the ASX. The State of Delaware does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize the CHESS system of holding securities or electronic transfers of legal title to shares. To enable companies to have their securities cleared and settled electronically through CHESS, depositary instruments called CHESS Depositary Interests (&#8220;CDIs&#8221;) are issued. CDIs are units of beneficial ownership in shares and are traded in a manner similar to shares of Australian companies listed on the ASX. The legal title to the shares is held by a depositary, CHESS Depositary Nominees Pty Ltd (&#8220;CDN&#8221;), which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the ASX, and is an approved general participant of ASX Settlement. One share of common stock is equivalent to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> CDI.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i><b>Dividend Rights</b></i>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Subject to the prior rights of holders of all classes of stock at the time outstanding having prior rights as to dividends, the holders of the common stock shall be entitled to receive, out of any assets of the Corporation legally available therefore, any dividends as <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be declared from time to time by the Board of Directors. The right to such dividends shall <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be cumulative, and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> right shall accrue by reason of the fact that dividends are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> declared in any prior period.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i><b>Voting Rights</b></i>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The holder of each share of common stock shall have the right to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> vote for each such share, and shall be entitled to notice of any stockholders&#8217; meeting in accordance with the Bylaws of the Corporation, and shall be entitled to vote upon such matters and in such manner as <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be provided by law.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i><b>Stock Option Plans</b></i> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 14, 2019, </em>the Board of Directors adopted, and our stockholders approved, the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> Equity Incentive Plan, reserving <ix:nonFraction id="c149068021" contextRef="i_2019-02-14_PlanNameAxis-The2019PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11,418,500</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock for the granting of incentive and nonqualified stock options, or other stock-based awards, to employees, directors, and consultants. On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 24, 2026, </em>the Board of Directors adopted, and on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 7, 2026, </em>our stockholders approved, the Amended and Restated <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> Equity Incentive Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">"2019</em> Plan") increasing the number of shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock reserved for issuance to <ix:nonFraction id="c149068024" contextRef="i_2026-05-07_PlanNameAxis-The2019PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">45,150,000</ix:nonFraction>. Under the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> Plan, on the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> day of each of the Company&#8217;s fiscal years beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> the number of shares of Common Stock available for issuance from time to time under the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> Plan automatically will be increased by an amount equal to the lesser of (i) <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> percent (<ix:nonFraction id="c149068030" contextRef="i_2026-05-07_PlanNameAxis-The2019PlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="imri:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuancePercentIncrease" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">5</ix:nonFraction>%) of the aggregate number of shares reserved under this Plan on the last day of the immediately preceding fiscal year, and (ii) such number of shares determined by the Board (the &#8220;Annual Increase&#8221;). The maximum aggregate number of shares that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued upon the exercise of ISOs under the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> Plan <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed the initial limit cumulatively increased on each <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1 </em>beginning in <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> by the lesser of the Annual Increase for such year or <ix:nonFraction id="c149068034" contextRef="i_2026-05-07_PlanNameAxis-The2019PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="imri:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuanceMaximumYearlyAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares, unless the increase is approved by our stockholders. Certain increases to the share reserve have historically received stockholder approval in connection with the Company&#8217;s annual meeting. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>, the cumulative number of shares authorized for issuance under the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> Plan is <ix:nonFraction id="c149068036" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_PlanNameAxis-The2019PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">45,150,000</ix:nonFraction> shares, of which <ix:nonFraction id="c149068037" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_PlanNameAxis-The2019PlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,940,887</ix:nonFraction> shares remained available for future issuance.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Options are granted at a price equal to the closing sale price of a CDI as of the date of grant, converted from Australian dollars to U.S. dollars using the prevailing exchange rate. Generally, vesting terms of outstanding options range from immediate to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068038">four</span> years. In addition, some options have been issued to the management team that vest upon completion of certain milestones and performance requirements; as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c149068039" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_PlanNameAxis-The2019PlanMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-ManagementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsOutstandingNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">26,393,261</ix:nonFraction> of these options are issued and outstanding. For these performance-based awards, expense is recognized over the requisite&#160;service&#160;period when it is probable the performance condition will be achieved. If at any point the Company determines that the performance condition is improbable, any previously recognized expense is reversed. Adjustments for forfeitures are recorded as they occur. In <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> event are the options exercisable for more than <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068041">ten</span> years after the date of grant. The Company issues new shares of common stock when stock options are exercised.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company reviews its current assumptions on a periodic basis and adjusts them as necessary to determine the option valuation. The expected term reflects our estimate of the period over which the stock options will remain outstanding before exercise or expiration. As we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have sufficient historical exercise data to provide a reasonable basis upon which to estimate the expected term, the expected term of stock option awards granted has been determined using the simplified method, which is the average of the weighted-average vesting period and the contractual term. Volatility is based on the Company&#8217;s own historical volatility as well as historic volatilities of traded shares from a selected publicly traded peer group, believed to be comparable after consideration of size, maturity, profitability, growth, risk and return on investment. The risk-free interest rate is based on the yield of constant maturity U.S. treasury bonds with a remaining term equal to the expected life of the awards at the grant date. The expected dividend yield is zero, as the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> paid or declared any dividends to common stockholders and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to pay dividends in the foreseeable future. The Company&#8217;s policy is to account for forfeitures as they occur and records stock-based compensation expense only for those awards that are expected to vest.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The warrants issued in connection with the equity raises were evaluated under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">480</em> and ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815.</em> Of the <ix:nonFraction id="c149068085" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-EquityRaiseWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="imri:ClassOfWarrantOrRightIssuedDuringPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">3,265,318</ix:nonFraction> warrants issued in connection with the equity raises, <ix:nonFraction id="c149068086" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-EquityRaiseWarrantsLiabilityClassifiedMember" unitRef="Share" name="imri:ClassOfWarrantOrRightIssuedDuringPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,100,568</ix:nonFraction> were determined to qualify as liabilities due to the exercise price being denominated in a currency other than the Company&#8217;s functional currency, while the remaining <ix:nonFraction id="c149068087" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-EquityRaiseWarrantsNonliabilityClassifiedMember" unitRef="Share" name="imri:ClassOfWarrantOrRightIssuedDuringPeriod" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,164,750</ix:nonFraction> do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the characteristics for liability classification under either provision and as such are classified as equity under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815.</em> The warrants expire <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068090">ten</span> years after the dates of issuance. In addition, the Company has <ix:nonFraction id="c149068091" contextRef="i_2026-06-30_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-SpaWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightOutstanding" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,950,840</ix:nonFraction> warrants outstanding that were issued in connection with the convertible notes (related party) issuances, which are classified as equity under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815.</em> See Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em> for further details.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> </b>&#8211;<b> Income Taxes</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The effective tax rate for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068101"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068171">zero</span></span> percent. As a result of the analysis of all available evidence as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company recorded a full valuation allowance on its net deferred tax assets. Consequently, the Company reported <ix:nonFraction id="c149068102" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-06-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> income tax benefit during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>. If the Company&#8217;s assumptions change and the Company believes that it will be able to realize these deferred tax assets, the tax benefits relating to any reversal of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets will be recognized as a reduction of future income tax expense. If the assumptions do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> change, each period the Company could record an additional valuation allowance on any increases in the deferred tax assets.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em> </b>&#8211;<b> Segment Information</b> </p>
   <p style="font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;font-size:9pt;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company sells capital equipment, which includes both Imricor-developed and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party equipment, and consumable products, for use in iCMR labs, and capital equipment maintenance service agreements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise about which separate discrete financial information is available for evaluation by the Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) when making decisions regarding resource allocation and assessing performance. The Company&#8217;s CODM is its Chief Executive Officer, who reviews consolidated financial results when making resource allocation decisions or evaluating Company performance. The Company manages its business on a consolidated basis and operates as <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068108"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c149068173">one</span></span> reportable segment, and the CODM&#8217;s primary measure of segment profit or loss is net loss.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">For the Company&#8217;s single reportable segment, the total amounts of segment profit or loss and segment assets are the same as net loss and total assets, respectively, presented in the accompanying unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;&#8195;</p>

We use words such as &#8220;will,&#8221; &#8220;may,&#8221; &#8220;expect,&#8221; &#8220;intend,&#8221; &#8220;seek,&#8221; &#8220;would,&#8221; &#8220;should,&#8221; &#8220;could,&#8221; &#8220;continue,&#8221; &#8220;plan,&#8221; &#8220;estimate,&#8221; &#8220;anticipate,&#8221; &#8220;believe,&#8221; and similar expressions to identify forward-looking statements, but the absence of these words does not mean that a statement is not forward looking.</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Overview</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Imricor is a U.S.-based medical device company that is leading the new field of real-time iCMR cardiac ablations &#8211; that is, cardiac ablations guided by real-time MR, rather than by conventional x-ray fluoroscopy. Our principal focus is the design, manufacturing, sale, and distribution of MR-compatible products for cardiac catheter ablation procedures.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Vision-MR Ablation Catheter is our prime product offering, specifically designed to work under real-time MR guidance, with the intent of enabling higher success rates along with a faster and safer treatment compared to conventional procedures using x-ray guided catheters. The Vision-MR Ablation Catheter has been approved in the European Union ("EU"), Qatar, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia ("KSA") with an indication for treating Type I atrial flutter. We also have approval for the sale of our capital product, the Advantage-MR EP Recorder/Stimulator System, in the EU, Qatar, and KSA. We have approval for the sale of our capital product, the NorthStar Mapping System, in the EU, KSA, and the U.S.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">We are continuing enrollment in our Vision-MR Ablation of Atrial Flutter ("VISABL-AFL") clinical trial to support U.S. market entry of the Vision-MR Ablation Catheter and RF-5000 ablation generator system. In parallel with the clinical trial, we have secured market clearance from the FDA for the Vision-MR Diagnostic Catheter and NorthStar Mapping System. We are pursuing approvals for our other products, including the Advantage-MR EP Recorder/Stimulator System and the Vision-MR Dispersive Electrode, while the VISABL-AFL clinical trial is ongoing.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">We sell our capital and consumable products to hospitals and clinics for use in iCMR labs, in which ablation procedures using the Vision-MR Ablation Catheter can be performed. We collaborate with GE Healthcare, Philips, and Siemens, the three leading global MR vendors who provide MR systems for iCMR labs, to target certain sites and support the design and construction of iCMR labs for those sites.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Financial overview</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Imricor is in the early commercialization phase and is not yet profitable as we continue to invest in clinical validation, regulatory approvals, and commercial infrastructure to support adoption of iCMR procedures. As a result, for the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company incurred a net loss of $25,139 thousand on revenues of $25 thousand. Operating expenses, primarily in research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative functions, reflect planned investments in pursuing U.S. regulatory approval, expanding our clinical support and sales teams, and building iCMR lab infrastructure in our target markets.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of&#160;June 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $60,539 thousand and marketable securities of $6,922 thousand, compared to cash and cash equivalents of $19,502 thousand and marketable securities of $21,278 thousand as of&#160;December 31, 2025. We have funded our operations to date primarily through the sale of our common stock and CDIs and through indebtedness. We expect to continue to incur operating losses for the foreseeable future as we execute our commercialization and clinical strategies. We anticipate that achieving profitability will require significant growth in iCMR procedure volume and geographic expansion, and the Company may require additional financing to support these objectives.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

These factors include:</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Recent Developments</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">On May 7, 2026, we completed a placement in which we issued 32,432,433 CDIs. We raised $41,586&#160;thousand in net proceeds after deducting issuance costs. Proceeds from this placement will support our growth strategy and may be used for purposes including launching the NorthStar Mapping System in the U.S., advancing regulatory approvals, completing clinical trials, research and development activities, and associated offer costs. For details of these securities offerings, see Part II, Item 2, &#8220;Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds.&#8221;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">On July 6, 2026, a total of&#160;5,051,539&#160;CDI options were exercised by holders of previously issued CDI options. We received total proceeds of approximately $2,100 thousand, net of expenses. &#160;In connection with the exercise, the fair value of the option liabilities of approximately $4,300 thousand as of the settlement date was reclassified to additional paid-in capital.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Components of our Consolidated Results of Operations</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Revenues</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">We generate revenue from product sales and service revenue. Revenue is recognized when control of the product or service transfers to the customer. For product sales that contain a single performance obligation, revenue is recognized at a point in time when title to the goods and risk of loss transfers to the customer, which typically occurs upon shipment. For product sales that contain multiple performance obligations, such as equipment sales that include installation services, we allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation based on the estimated or observable standalone selling price and recognize revenue for each performance obligation when (or as) control is transferred to the customer and the performance obligation is satisfied. Service revenue is recognized over time as services are provided. Sales tax and value added taxes in foreign jurisdictions that are collected from customers and remitted to governmental authorities are accounted for on a net basis and therefore are excluded from net sales. Product sales include shipping and handling fees charged to customers. Shipping and handling costs associated with outbound freight after control over a product has transferred to a customer are accounted for as a fulfillment cost and are included in cost of goods sold.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Product Revenue</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our product revenue is derived from sales of our cardiac ablation systems, associated consumables, and third-party equipment to hospitals, clinics, and other providers. Our primary products include the Vision-MR Ablation Catheter and Vision-MR Diagnostic Catheter, which are used in iCMR-guided ablation procedures. Customers select our products based on clinical efficacy, ease of use, pricing, and third-party reimbursement availability. We currently derive revenue from international markets, particularly the European Union, where we maintain a direct sales organization. In other international markets, including the Middle East, we distribute our products through exclusive distributors. We evaluate sales returns and allowances for variable consideration on a monthly basis and allowance for credit losses at each reporting period. We have historically not considered provisions for these items necessary.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Service Revenue</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our service revenue is derived from service agreements for maintenance on our Advantage-MR EP Recorder/Stimulator System and third-party equipment products provided to hospitals, clinics, and other providers. Service revenue is recognized over the contract period on a straight-line basis as customers benefit from the services throughout the service contract period.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Costs and Expenses</b> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Costs of Goods Sold</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Cost of goods sold represents costs directly related to production and distribution of our products, including raw materials and components, manufacturing labor, quality assurance testing, product sterilization and packaging, shipping and handling costs, and manufacturing overhead. Shipping and handling costs associated with outbound freight after control over a product has transferred to a customer are accounted for as a fulfillment cost and are included in cost of goods sold. Manufacturing overhead costs include the cost of material procurement, inventory control, and equipment and operations supervision. Cost of goods sold also includes depreciation expense for product tooling, production equipment, and equipment placed at customer sites as part of commercial sales agreements. Costs associated with any inventory write-downs resulting from quarterly physical inventory counts and product obsolescence are also included within cost of goods sold. Fluctuations in our cost of goods sold correspond with the fluctuations in these costs as well as sales volume.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i>Sales and Marketing</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Sales and marketing expenses consist primarily of sales and marketing personnel, field sales travel, trade show expenses, physician training and education programs, and consultant fees related to market development and commercialization strategy. We anticipate that our sales and marketing expenses will increase as we expand our direct sales force in the U.S. and EU, establish and support international distribution partnerships, and increase marketing investments to drive adoption of our MR-guided ablation systems.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i>Research and Development Expenses</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Research and development include salaries for our research and development, regulatory, quality, and clinical personnel, clinical trial expenses, regulatory submissions, manufacturing process improvements, product development costs, enhancements to our currently commercialized products, and additional investments in our product development pipeline. We expense research and development expenses as incurred. We track external costs on a development program basis for our key programs, including VISABL-AFL and Vision-MR Ablation of Ventricular Tachycardia ("VISABL-VT"). However, we do not track internal costs, including personnel related costs, equipment costs, facility costs, and supplies, on a development program basis because these costs are deployed across multiple programs and are monitored in total rather than by individual program. We generally expect that research and development expenses will increase as we conduct our VISABL-AFL and VISABL-VT clinical trials, pursue additional regulatory approvals in the U.S. and international markets, advance next-generation product development, and optimize our manufacturing processes.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i>General and Administrative Expenses</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">General and administrative expenses consist primarily of salaries for our executive, finance, accounting, and human resources personnel; share-based compensation; professional fees for accounting, audit, legal, and tax services; public company compliance costs; directors and officers liability insurance; and facility costs. We anticipate general and administrative expenses will increase as we hire additional personnel to support growth in our commercial and research and development teams, comply with SEC reporting requirements, and enhance our internal systems and controls infrastructure.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"><i>Other Income (Expense)</i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Other income (expense) consists primarily of changes in fair value of our financial instruments, including convertible notes (related party), option liabilities, and warrant liabilities that are remeasured to fair value at each reporting period, as well as interest income from our investments in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Additionally, other income and expense may include foreign currency exchange gains and losses resulting from remeasurements on our cash holdings, receivables, and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies such as Euros and Australian dollars, government grant income related to our research and development activities, and interest expense on financing agreements.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Cost of Goods Sold</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Costs of goods sold during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, were $733&#160;thousand, compared to $510&#160;thousand during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $223 thousand. The increase in cost of goods sold was primarily due to higher personnel-related costs compared to the prior period. Personnel-related costs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, and other employee expenses, increased $307 thousand following the expansion of our manufacturing and quality assurance teams which resulted in&#160;a higher number of employees during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026,&#160;compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025. Additionally, other operating expenses increased $94 thousand, primarily driven by increased non-recurring engineering and product testing costs. These increases were partially offset by a $153 thousand favorable change in inventory absorption resulting from higher production levels, including production of clinical trial materials and equipment, relative to sales during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Sales and Marketing</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Sales and marketing expenses during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, were $1,647&#160;thousand, compared to $1,127&#160;thousand during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $520 thousand. This increase was primarily attributed to higher event-related sales and marketing expenses of $444 thousand, driven by increased spending for trade shows, conventions and related marketing materials. Additionally, travel expenses, including airfare and lodging costs associated with field demonstrations and customer engagement, increased&#160;$83 thousand during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026&#160;compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Research and Development</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Research and development expenses during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, were $3,676&#160;thousand, compared to $2,857&#160;thousand during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $819 thousand. This increase was primarily attributed to higher personnel-related costs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, and other employee expenses, which increased $563 thousand, due to a higher number of research and development employees during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026,&#160;compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025, to support multiple concurrent development programs and regulatory initiatives. Additionally, external clinical expenses increased $281 thousand, reflecting expanded clinical trial activities, driven by an increase of $215 thousand in external costs associated with the VISABL-AFL trial, as new hospitals join the clinical trial. Professional services, including consulting expenses, increased $117 thousand, primarily to support these development programs, regulatory initiatives, and clinical trial activities. These increases were partially offset by a decrease in prototype and testing expenses of $144 thousand.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>General and Administrative</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">General and administrative expenses during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, were $1,430&#160;thousand, compared to $1,263&#160;thousand during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $167 thousand. This increase was primarily attributed to higher professional services, including audit and legal expenses, which increased $150 thousand, primarily due to additional audit and compliance requirements associated with SEC registration and reporting obligations. Furthermore, personnel-related costs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, and other employee expenses, increased $51 thousand due to a higher number of general and administrative employees during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026,&#160;compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025, to support the additional reporting obligations associated with the SEC registration and growth in personnel in preparation for anticipated U.S. commercialization following expected FDA approval.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Other Income (Expense)</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Total other income (expense) during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, was income of $43&#160;thousand, compared to an expense of $2,103 thousand during the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2025, representing a decrease in expense of $2,146 thousand. This decrease was primarily attributed to lower non-cash expenses from changes in fair value of convertible notes (related party), option liabilities, and warrant liabilities, which together decreased from expense of $3,999 thousand for the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2025, to income of $386 thousand for the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, representing a favorable change of $4,385 thousand. This favorable change was partially offset by an unfavorable change in foreign currency exchange loss (gain) of $1,969 thousand, primarily related to foreign currency remeasurement on our cash held in Australian dollars.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Net loss</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">As a result of the above factors, our net loss was $7,382 thousand for the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to a net loss of $7,795 thousand for the&#160;three months ended June 30, 2025. We expect to continue incurring net losses until such time as we obtain additional regulatory approvals for our MR-compatible cardiac catheter ablation products, expand our commercialization, and generate sufficient revenue to offset our costs and expenses.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Revenues</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our revenue is derived from product revenue and service revenue. We earned revenue of&#160;$25&#160;thousand for the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026, as compared to revenue of&#160;$197&#160;thousand for the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2025, a decrease of $172 thousand. The decrease in revenue compared to the prior period was primarily due to a decrease in product revenue, resulting from lower&#160;sales volumes&#160;of consumable devices of $94 thousand and a customer return of consumable devices totaling $76 thousand. This customer return occurred during the three months ended March 31, 2026, and, as a result, revenues for the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026, are lower than revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">The decrease in sales volumes was primarily attributable to<b>&#160;</b>certain customer sites in Europe exclusively enrolling patients in our VISABL-AFL clinical trial. Consumable devices used in clinical trial procedures are not recognized as product revenue. During the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2025, patients treated at these sites were treated commercially, resulting in recognized product revenue. We currently expect that, following completion of enrollment in our VISABL-AFL clinical trial, these customer sites in the European Union will transition back to commercial use of our consumable devices, and based on our assessment, this trend is reasonably likely to have a favorable impact on future product revenue. The customer return of consumable devices reflects a one-time concession, and management does not expect customer returns to become a recurring or significant component of revenue adjustments. Service revenue remained relatively constant compared to the prior period, due to ongoing maintenance and support services provided to existing customers throughout the year.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Cost of Goods Sold</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Costs of goods sold during the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026, were $1,395&#160;thousand, compared to $812&#160;thousand during the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $583 thousand. The increase in cost of goods sold was primarily due to higher personnel-related costs compared to the prior period. Personnel-related costs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, and other employee expenses, increased $647 thousand following the expansion of our manufacturing and quality assurance teams which resulted in&#160;a higher number of employees during the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026,&#160;compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025. Additionally, other operating expenses increased $152 thousand, primarily driven by increased non-recurring engineering and product testing costs. These increases were partially offset by a $261 thousand favorable change in inventory absorption resulting from higher production levels, including production of clinical trial materials and equipment, relative to sales during the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i><b>Sales and Marketing</b></i> </p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">Sales and marketing expenses during the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026, were $2,820&#160;thousand, compared to $2,205&#160;thousand during the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of $615 thousand. This increase was primarily attributed to higher event-related sales and marketing expenses of $364 thousand, driven by increased spending for trade shows, conventions and related marketing materials. Additionally, there were higher travel expenses for field sales activities and personnel-related costs. Travel expenses, including airfare and lodging costs associated with field demonstrations and customer engagement, increased&#160;$144 thousand. Personnel-related costs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, and other employee expenses, increased&#160;$87 thousand, reflecting the expansion of our European sales team during 2025 which resulted in&#160;a higher number of sales employees during the&#160;six months ended June 30, 2026,&#160;compared to the corresponding period in&#160;2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:9pt;font-variant:normal;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;">&#160;</p>
